solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sergio's wild, wild parties

indicators.note: the first 'wild' says the name has run wild, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the name Sergio; the 's stands for 'is', joining it to the anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone called Sergio is out of control, and so are his parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'wild' does two jobs: the first scrambles SERGIO, the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgies are riotous, unrestrained celebrations, the very picture of wild parties.

clue.text: Definitely astray, ignoring one of two females

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so one letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: something astray has gone off course
F is the abbreviation for female, and the phrase for astray contains two of them

explanation.surface: Someone is sure they have lost their way and left one of two women behind.
explanation.walkthrough: OFF COURSE holds two Fs; dropping one leaves OF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Of course' is an emphatic yes, used just like 'definitely' to show certainty.

clue.text: Acquire wealth, almost adopting regressive attitude that's ancient

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is housed within the other
almost means the last letter is not reached and is dropped

parts.note: to acquire wealth is to get rich

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: A comment on someone getting rich while clinging to backward views that are positively antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter off the phrase; 'regressive' reverses the attitude word, and 'adopting' puts that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric is used informally of anything very old, a jokey synonym for ancient.

clue.text: Paradise discovered in neglected environment

indicators.note: found inside, so the answer is concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: A paradise turns up in an unlikely, run-down setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise, and the name stands for any perfect place.

clue.text: Put in the post, boxed by a worker, perhaps one not at work?

indicators.note: enclosed by, so one piece sits inside the others

parts.note: a worker bee, the classic crossword worker
something put in the post has been sent

explanation.surface: A letter mailed by an employee who is perhaps off sick.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone missing from where they should be, such as an employee off the job.

clue.text: Take issue, on reflection, and delay for something better

parts.note: to buy something is to take it in exchange for payment

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

explanation.surface: Someone objects, then thinks better of it and holds off hoping for a better deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take issue' looks like one idiom for arguing; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy time is to stall deliberately, gaining a delay in hope of improved circumstances.

clue.text: Ask chap to move right along for horses

indicators.note: the letter is told to shift its position within the word
it travels further along the word rather than leaving it

parts.note: to request is to ask
Ian, a man's name standing for any chap

explanation.surface: Someone asks a man to shift a little to make room for some horses.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter for 'right' travels along the word to sit just after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrian describes anything relating to horse riding, so it means 'for horses'.

clue.text: Greek character that's rambling around centre of Crete

indicators.note: these letters are placed around another letter
wandering about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word 'that'; the 's stands for 'is', joining it to the anagram signal

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A Greek person who wanders around the heart of Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' turns THAT into THTA; 'around' wraps it round E, the centre of Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, and 'character' here means a written letter.

clue.text: Saw psychic power that is source of disbelief

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception
i.e., the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

indicators.note: the source is where something starts, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A psychic's claimed powers are what make people doubt them.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, so espied is a past-tense synonym of saw.

clue.text: Mean, like a wasp?

definitions.meaning: playfully, '...' as in having a sting, as a wasp has

explanation.surface: Is a wasp a mean creature?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as sting + -y, 'having a sting'; the question mark flags the invented sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy is the usual word for someone tight-fisted, a direct synonym of mean.

clue.text: It's the job of a craftsman to criticise appearance

definitions.text: It's the job of a craftsman

parts.note: to carp is to find fault or criticise
an entry is an appearance, as of an actor coming on stage

explanation.surface: Someone claims that skilled workers exist to find fault with how things look.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is the trade of working wood, the work of a skilled woodworker.

clue.text: University organisation has no time to finish

indicators.note: the letter is lacking, so it is removed

parts.note: a setup is an arrangement or organisation

explanation.surface: A university body is running out of time to complete its business.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up something is to consume all of it, to finish it off.

clue.text: State bureau finally thanks hospital

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A government office ends by thanking a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: As pelicans move — very slowly

indicators.note: the letters are shifted about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A note that pelicans get about at a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at a snail's pace is an idiom for moving extremely slowly.

clue.text: Spooner's lavish course in Chelsea, for example

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: to shower is to lavish, give generously
to flow is to course, run like water

explanation.surface: A lavish course of study set in a smart part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOWER FLOW with its opening sounds swapped becomes FLOWER SHOW. The Chelsea Flower Show is the Royal Horticultural Society's famous annual show in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is the best-known example of a flower show, an exhibition of plants and gardens.

clue.text: Acutely unwise to retain personnel

indicators.note: to keep hold of, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: silly means foolish, unwise
HR, human resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: It would be a sharp mistake to keep the staff on.
explanation.definitionFit: Acutely here means in a high, piercing pitch, which is how something sounds when uttered shrilly.

clue.text: Regularly seen with high-calorie supplement

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: rich food is heavy and high in calories

explanation.surface: A high-calorie food supplement keeps cropping up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich something is to add to it and improve it, which is what supplementing does.

clue.text: Awfully sly act in river becomes a disaster

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Cam is the river that flows through Cambridge

indicators.note: done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sly bit of behaviour in a river ends in catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' scrambles SLY ACT to TACLYS, which goes 'in' CAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a sudden violent upheaval, a calamity on a large scale.

clue.text: Make new version of brake release

parts.note: a rein is a check or brake, as in keeping a rein on spending
to vent is to let out, release

explanation.surface: Someone is redesigning a vehicle's brake release.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvent something is to produce a fresh, changed form of it.

clue.text: Starts to see caged birds giving dirty looks

indicators.note: the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: owls are birds

explanation.surface: Birds in cages glaring at visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Scowls are angry frowning expressions, which is what a dirty look is.

clue.text: Bag fasteners swapping ends

indicators.note: exchanging places, so the second end letter goes to the opposite end
the end letters of the word are the ones that change places

parts.note: latches are fasteners on doors and gates

explanation.surface: A bag whose clasps have been switched around.
explanation.walkthrough: LATCHES with its first and last letters exchanged gives SATCHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, classically used to carry school books.

clue.text: Latte's prepared, enjoyed originally here?

indicators.note: made ready, so the letters are reworked into a new order
at the origin, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A city where people first made and drank lattes.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Seattle is home of the coffee-house chains that spread latte culture.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the birthplace of Starbucks and is famous for its coffee culture.

clue.text: Having a weapon is said to be immoral

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the answer sounds like this word

parts.note: sworded means equipped with a sword

explanation.surface: Carrying arms is called a wicked thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid means morally base or squalid, close in sense to immoral.

clue.text: Inflate balloon, at first depressed, then happy

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to feel low is to feel depressed
up means cheerful, in good spirits

explanation.surface: A child's mood swings as a balloon is filled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balloon' seems part of the definition with Inflate, but only gives B.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up a balloon or tyre is to inflate it with air.

clue.text: Starmer's lot not united — a Conservative finds room for investigation

indicators.note: the letter is excluded, so it is removed

parts.note: Keir Starmer leads the UK Labour Party
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political scene: a divided Labour, with a Tory finding space to probe.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room equipped for scientific experiments and research.

clue.text: Creature's home secured by appeal

definitions.note: the noun creature; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: held fast by, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: to beg is to appeal
in means at home

explanation.surface: An animal's home is kept safe through a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any living thing, so the word is a synonym of creature.

clue.text: Have a quick look at small container

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a can is a metal container

explanation.surface: Someone takes a glance at a little tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a page is to glance over it rapidly, looking quickly.

clue.text: Junkie's guide — no heroin

definitions.note: the noun junkie; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

indicators.note: the letter is absent, so it is taken out

parts.note: an usher guides people to their seats
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A guide for addicts that warns off heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for a drug addict, a synonym of junkie.

clue.text: Consider value of soldier in cut back

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to hew is to cut with an axe
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Pondering what a soldier is worth after spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: GI 'in' HEW makes HGIEW, which 'back' reverses to WEIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh something up is to assess its worth or importance.

clue.text: Bob, for example, exercising this early?

indicators.note: putting through a workout, so the letters are worked into new positions

explanation.surface: Someone named Bob is doing his morning workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut of even length, one example of a hairstyle.

clue.text: Kitchen waste — who's going to eat it?

definitions.meaning: the reply is '...', run together as one word

explanation.surface: Someone holds up kitchen scraps and asks who will eat them.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a question whose answer, 'pigs will', reads as the single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is leftover food and kitchen scraps fed to pigs.

clue.text: Instigate concert training

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms
PT, physical training

explanation.surface: Someone sets up rehearsals for a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt is to provoke or cause something to happen, as instigating does.
